newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME live cattle end up on USDA report.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME live cattle end up on USDA report.

text.p: Nearby CME live cattle futures ended higher on Friday's mildly bullish USDA Cattle-on-Feed report in generally quiet activity, traders said.
Feeder cattle futures finished lower on pressure from higher corn futures, traders said.

December paced the gain in nearby live cattle after Friday's cattle data showed July placements at 106 percent of a year ago, well under the average estimate of 110.5 percent. October traded both sides of previous levels but ended up on demand from a firm tone to cash markets, they said.
Deferred months eased on expectations that following placements on feed would rise, sources said.

Spreaders bought December and sold October and February except Rosenthal Collins which bought February and sold October, traders said. R.J. O'Brien was a late buyer in October. RBH turned a buyer in October after selling early and added demand from ADM pushed prices up into buy stops. However, prices eased back as renewed profit taking developed. December showed general demand from the report, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, volatility in October was down about 1-1/2 with general selling of October 70 calls on the rally in futures keeping the premium down. There was some selling of April and June 72 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures showed initial support on the cattle report but quickly slipped when live cattle traded mixed and corn futures rose, traders said.

Selling by Lind-Waldock and LFG pressed October early while E.D.&F. Man sold September, traders said. Refco sold October late against buying by LFG and local covering. RBH bought October feeders and sold October live cattle, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.475 cent higher to 0.075 lower with October up 0.175 at 71.175 cents a lb. Feeders ended up 0.025 to off 0.675 with October off 0.550 at 62.825 cents a lb.
